title: KV sidecar orchestrator and proportional connection-pool shedding playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background:
Redwood's serving runtime increasingly hits tail latency and saturation on downstream stores (Redis, Kafka, primary DB) during bursty multi-region spikes. Current single-knob circuit breakers and binary failover cause large step-changes in success rate and customer latency. We need a coordinated, gradual degradation strategy that operates at the connection-pool level, can be scoped per-tenant and per-region, and integrates with our SLO-driven routing decisions.

Goal:
Design, implement, and document a KV-sidecar orchestrator and a proportional connection-pool shedding strategy with the following properties:
1) Smooth degradation curve: reduce requests to a stressed dependency proportionally instead of immediate cutoff.
2) Per-tenant QoS lanes: respect tenant priorities when shedding (gold/silver/free).
3) Multi-region awareness: prefer regional fallbacks with weighted hedging; avoid global failover unless regional circuits are saturated.
4) Observability & safety: expose metrics, rollout flags, and automated canary that verifies no SLO regression across a 48-72 hour window before wide rollout.

Proposed design (high level):
- KV Sidecar Orchestrator: a lightweight control plane process colocated with runtime nodes that manages local connection pools to downstreams. Responsibilities: dynamic pool resizing, token-bucket admission with tenant weights, and issuing graded circuit signals (green/yellow/red) based on local latency/error windows. Sidecar publishes socket-level telemetry to the Console via existing traces and new metrics (pool_utilization, shed_rate_by_tenant, avg_kv_latency_p50/95/99).
- Proportional ConnPool Shedding: when a dependency shows stress (e.g., >p95 latency threshold or >X% 5xxs), sidecar computes a shedding factor S in [0,1] based on distance from healthy baseline. Incoming requests sampled and admitted with probability (1 - S * tenant_backoff_factor). Tenant_backoff_factor defaults to 1.0 but for higher tiers uses 0.2-0.5. This produces smooth probability-based shedding rather than hard rejects.
- Scoped Fallbacks & Hedging: requests that are shed for a primary dependency are routed to (a) cached KV prefix if available, (b) regional replica, or (c) degraded response path (empty-safe default) with a marker in the response metadata. Hedging to fallback targets is rate-limited and uses exponentially-weighted bloom estimation to avoid cascading to already saturated replicas.
- Circuit signaling & escalation: sidecar aggregates short-window stats and signals a regional coordinator if >N nodes report yellow for same dependency. Coordinator can escalate throttling, start cross-region hedging, or trigger capacity alerts. Full global circuit (binary open) only after 3 escalation steps and manual override disabled by default.

Trade-offs considered:
- Probabilistic shedding increases variability in per-request fate which may complicate debugging. Mitigation: add deterministic per-tenant hashing override for debugging and deterministic replay in traces.
- Early hedging may increase load on replicas; we mitigate with adaptive weight decay and probe-based hedging that backs off when replicas show increased load.
- Sidecar complexity vs. central orchestration: sidecar keeps fast local reaction times and reduces global orchestration latency; central coordinator handles cross-node coordination and long-window decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- System can reduce successful traffic to a stressed Redis instance by up to 80% within 5s of detection with no cascade failures on replicas.
- No SLO regression beyond 1% increase in p99 latency for gold-tier tenants during 72-hour canary under controlled fault injection.
- Metrics surfaced in Console: shed_rate, pool_utilization, admitted_rate_by_tenant, fallback_rate, and coordinator_escalations with dashboards and alerts.
- A runnable chaos test and a GitHub PR with sidecar and runtime integration that passes e2e.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement sidecar + local connpool hooks behind a feature flag (dev-only).
2) Unit tests + integration tests against a local Redis/Kafka mock harness.
3) Canary rollout 5% of serving nodes in staging with synthetic load generator.
4) Controlled chaos in staging: simulate 2x p95 latency and 2x error-rate for primary dependency. Validate metrics and safe degrade.
5) Gradual prod canary: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 48-72 hours with rollback gated by SLO monitors.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Throttling thresholds (default values) and learning period for baseline metrics. Proposal: use rolling 10-minute baseline and 1-minute reaction window.
- Tenant weight defaults and admin UI in Console to tune per-customer QoS lanes.
- Persistent vs ephemeral state for sidecar (on restart it should rehydrate minimal metadata).
- Failure handling when sidecar crashes: runtime must revert to conservative default pooling (no shedding) to avoid accidental mass-deny.

- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/KV+Sidecar+Orchestrator
- Spike PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6221
- Chaos scenarios: https://github.com/redwood-inference/chaos-runbooks/blob/main/kv-sidecar.md
- Observability dashboard (Console ticket): console-1482

2026-03-11 Mateo Chen: Implemented draft of local token-bucket admission and tenant weighting. Submitted spike PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6221. Requesting review from @Priya and @Jules.

2026-03-11 Priya Kapoor: Reviewed PR, suggested deterministic hashing fallback for easier debugging and added notes on metrics labels to ensure per-tenant cardinality control. Asked to avoid high-cardinality tags in metrics.

2026-03-12 Jules Ortega (SRE): Ran quick staging test injecting 2x p95 on Redis-primary. Sidecar reduced admitted_rate to primary by ~64% within 7s, fallback hit increased to replica but within acceptable limits. Documented observations in chaos-runbook. Recommend tweaking decay constant on hedging weights.
2026-03-12 Mateo Chen: Updated PR with deterministic-hash override and lowered default tenant_backoff_factor for gold tenants to 0.25. Planning telemetry PR next.
